messages.author: a6427b681690bc4e
messages.subject: Chi-square significant
parts:
My Chi-square test is always 0,00, but my model has a good fit looking into the other indicators. What can I do about this? Even if I respecify my model, the difference stays significant. And can I report such a model in a scientific paper? Or is this not done?
Thanks!

messages.author: af82fa98896529e2
messages.subject: Re: Chi-square significant
parts:
I believe that you have a saturated model, such as one-factor model with three indicators. If the model is saturated, df will be 0. You cannot use chi-square test to investigate whether your model fits the data well. The best thing you can do is to take a look at the magnitude of all parameter estimates, as well as its significance testing.

Different journals have different standards in publishing SEM results. I cannot answer it.

messages.author: 0325c6a976085eab
messages.subject: Re: Chi-square significant
parts:
The chi-square statistic, or the p-value.

If you're talking about the p-value, the reason that other measures of fit were developed was because the chi-square test is often significant, and does not tell you about the size of the misfit.  

So yes, if you're talking about the p-value, you can report the model. Read some papers that use SEM, and you'll find this.

messages.subject: Re: Chi-square significant
parts:
No matter report a model in a scientific paper with chi-square's p-value is zero if your model is valid by another model fit indices. :)

You can check Model Fit Indices with fitmeasures() function in lavaan.
